summary: Jan Safarewicz was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Vilnius University and studied at the University of Paris under Émile Benveniste and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Vilnius University and Jagiellonian University.

Jan Szczepan Otrębski worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Warsaw, Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, August Leskien, and Karl Brugmann, and Jagiellonian University under Jan Michał Rozwadowski. He held posts at Jagiellonian, Vilnius, and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Jan T. Ergardt worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson and received his Ph.D. from Lund University, where he was also attested in 1989.

Jan Westerhoff works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Cambridge, studying under Michael Potter, and SOAS. His academic posts include positions at CUNY, Linacre College, Durham University, SOAS, Lady Margaret Hall, and the University of Oxford.
Jan Wilhelm Boissevain was an Indologist. He earned his PhD at Leiden University between circa 1898 and 1905 under the supervision of Jacob Samuel Speyer.

Jan Willem de Jong was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Leiden, Harvard, and Paris, supervised by Jan Gonda and Frederik David Kan Bosch. He held positions at Leiden University and Australian National University.

Jan de Vries was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University, and studied under Willibald Kirfel. He held a post at Leiden University from 1926 to 1946.

Jan van der Valk works in Tibetology and Indology. He completed an MSc in biology at KU Leuven and a PhD in anthropology at the University of Kent. From 2018 to 2024, he was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Vienna.

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. His posts include positions at Hamburg, Munich, the University of Copenhagen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Ruhr University Bochum.
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied as a pupil under Surendranath Dasgupta. He held an attested post at Jadavpur University in 1977.
Janardan Mishra worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Director of the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning, with posts attested in 1959 and 1987.
Jane Bunnag was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of London by 1969, supervised by E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and as a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar in religious studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College and Newnham College, Cambridge, learning under Robert Alexander Neil, and later held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1898 to 1922.

Jane Helen Rowlands was an Indologist and linguist. She studied at Bangor University, Newnham College, Cambridge, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Paris (Sorbonne), where she earned a Ph.D. She later taught English at Karimganj College.
Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She has held positions at Cornell University, including Director of Graduate Studies and Associate Professor.

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley. She has held posts at Stony Brook, Wesleyan, Amherst College, and as Hershey Professor at Harvard University.

Janet R. Goodwin specializes in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and later held posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.
Jang-Kil Chun works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chun studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Frances Wilson, and doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota.

Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Cornell and Columbia under Alex Wayman and Thubten Yeshe. She served as Professor at Wesleyan University from 1977 to 2013 and taught at Agnes Scott College.
